answer: Tie each identity to a kernel only it can run. Each applicant receives a tiny virtual machine whose opcode table is shuffled uniquely for that identity, plus a prism of probe programs exercising every opcode. The applicant must write an interpreter for that kernel, then pass a live beacon: a program broadcast at a random hour that only its interpreter runs correctly within ten minutes. Each fake costs about 30 hours of skilled work; 10,000 fakes cost 300,000 hours, and no interpreter transfers, since each opcode table differs, so bulk hiring buys no shortcut.
